rule.title: Mandatory Architectural Decision Records (ADR) for Structural Decisions
rule.statement: Any structural architectural decision that introduces new database engines, external protocols, communication patterns, or alters boundary contracts must be documented in a committed Architectural Decision Record (ADR).
rule.rationale: Architectural intent and trade-off rationales fade from team memory over time. Undocumented decisions lead to repeated debates and accidental architectural regression.
rule.implementation_guidance: Record decisions under docs/adr/NNNN-title.md containing: Title, Status, Context, Decision, and Consequences (positive and negative trade-offs).

forbidden.example: Switching from REST to WebSockets or adopting Redis without a documented ADR discussing connection scale and infrastructure costs.

preferred.example: docs/adr/0004-use-pgvector-for-rag-embeddings.md documenting why pgvector was selected over standalone vector DBs.

source.evidence_quote: An Architectural Decision Record (ADR) captures an important architectural decision made along with its context and consequences. It provides lasting documentation of architectural intent.
